resolvedFailures.criterion: Round nineteen: every sentence of the data home's exemption is sourced in the code it describes — the architect's own flag, that `Oh My Pi puts its whole profile root under $XDG_DATA_HOME/omp where that directory exists` might be an inference dressed as a fact in the paragraph where this branch has spent the night punishing exactly that.
resolvedFailures.evidence: It was an inference, and sourcing it showed two different things wrong. What I found, measured: `ompdirs.xdgCandidate` builds the candidate as `$XDG_DATA_HOME/omp` for the default profile and `$XDG_DATA_HOME/omp/profiles/<name>` for a named one, and `xdgRoot` answers it as the profile root only where it already exists; every Legion role runs the named profile `legion` (`OMP_PROFILE`, operatorpod.go:23, read by `profileOf`). A throwaway test calling `ompdirs.ProfileRoot` under exactly a role container's environment gave three results: no candidate, root `<HOME>/.omp/profiles/legion` on the container filesystem; `data/omp/profiles/legion` present, root that path on the volume; a bare `data/omp` present, root back on the container filesystem. So the sentence's condition named a directory whose existence does not produce the effect it described. What the implementer then found, which is the larger half and which I had not: the directories that sentence was really about — `run/daemons`, `logs`, `browser-profiles`, `reports`, `terminal-sessions` — hang under `$XDG_STATE_HOME/omp`, not the data home (podsafety.go:137-140, `sessions are data-class` in the same parenthesis), so the reason belonged to the per-role state home the paragraph already exempts.
resolvedFailures.verifiedHow: Re-verified at the new head rather than taken. The state-class sentence is now attached to `/legion/scratch/state/<role>` and is the code's own list, and this volume agrees: `/legion/scratch/state/tester/omp/profiles/legion` exists, each role's state home is 16K, and the data home is 4.0K. The data home's exemption now rests on `nothing re-derives it`, which is checkable against the rest of the list — cache, tmp and the install cache are rebuilt by the next build or install, a data home is not. The paragraph makes no size claim about the data home at all, which is right: every reading anyone has is from pods on the merge-base layout, which are told no XDG_DATA_HOME, so 4.0K is evidence for nothing. The enumeration still passes at the new head, 9 of 9.

resolvedFailures.evidence: `internal/shim` does not run under the TMPDIR this change gives a role container. In this issue's tester container, at the branch's code head, `cd packages/daemon && TMPDIR=/legion/scratch/implementer/tmp go test -count=1 -p 1 ./internal/shimwire/ ./internal/shim/ ./internal/stream/` fails with 16 `bind: invalid argument` listens, every one of them a socket this package's own helper spells under TMPDIR — for example `listen on /legion/scratch/implementer/tmp/TestAdoptWorkingCopyRunsTheSharedMetaeditAndAnswersTheDaemona_c240954141/003/s: bind: invalid argument` (shim_test.go:963), 110 bytes against Linux's 107-byte sun_path. The same command with TMPDIR=/tmp, which is what a role container had before this change (it was told no temporary directory at all), passes; `internal/shimwire` and `internal/stream` pass under both, and `cmd/legion` passes under both because this pull request already fixed it there (socketDir, worker_shim_test.go). So this is a regression this change introduces, in the same class the implementer recognised and fixed in one package: `internal/shim/shim_test.go:388`'s `socketPath` is `filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "s")`, the exact helper the pull request replaced in cmd/legion. The pull request's `Fast-follow:` line names `internal/daemon/daemon_test.go`'s `shortTempDir` and `internal/stream/helpers_test.go`'s `shortSocketPath` as the remaining copies; both of those in fact bind (stream's whole suite passes under the production TMPDIR), and the package that actually breaks is named nowhere. A defect that breaks a gate is not a fast-follow. Red test, in its own commit on this branch: `packages/daemon/internal/shim/socketpath_test.go`, `TestASocketPathBindsWhereTMPDIRIsARoleContainersScratch` — it points TMPDIR at a directory as long as a role container's and listens on the path `socketPath` builds, and fails today on any machine, CI included: `cd packages/daemon && go test -count=1 -run TestASocketPathBindsWhereTMPDIRIsARoleContainersScratch ./internal/shim/` prints `listen on /tmp/73b92639f15805283e38c12e76/TestASocketPathBindsWhereTMPDIRIsARoleContainersScratchAdoptWor2572775919/001/s (111 bytes): bind: invalid argument`. Rooting this package's socket directory at /tmp the way cmd/legion's socketDir does makes it pass.
resolvedFailures.notReproducedHere: `internal/daemon` could not be judged: its suite needs Docker (testcontainers panics `rootless Docker not found`) and a role container has none. Its `shortTempDir` builds `<TMPDIR>/lgdXXXXXXXXX/worker-stream.sock`, about 63 bytes under the rendered TMPDIR, so arithmetic says it fits; CI is where it is actually exercised, and CI runs with a short TMPDIR, so nothing here proves it either way.
